findings.location: source.html paragraph 2 ("In some places, like the Palatinate...")
findings.source_quote: In the mid-1600s, the local Prince, Elector Ludwig, invited the exiled Swiss Brethren into the Palatinate to help rebuild the farms because of their reputation as excellent husbandmen and tillers of the soil.
findings.suggested_fix: Capitalize the sentence-initial letter in the corresponding translation paragraph so it reads "A mediados de 1600, el príncipe local, el elector Ludwig, invitó..." (preserve existing HTML tags and attributes).
findings.translation_quote: a mediados de 1600, el príncipe local, el elector Ludwig, invitó a los Hermanos Suizos exiliados al Palatinado para ayudar a reconstruir las granjas debido a su reputación como excelentes agricultores y labradores de la tierra.

findings.location: source.html paragraph 7 ("Also elk, timber bison, and whitetail deer...")
findings.source_quote: There were also elk, timber bison, and whitetail deer in abundance (which were glad to eat whatever the settlers planted).
findings.suggested_fix: Use a more natural Spanish rendering of "timber bison"—for example, "bisonte de las madera" is also awkward; better: "bisonte norteño" or "bisonte" depending on target readership. Suggested translated phrase: "También abundaban alces, bisontes y ciervos de cola blanca (los cuales estaban más que dispuestos a comer lo que los colonos plantaban)." Preserve HTML tags and paragraph structure.
findings.translation_quote: También había alces, bisonte de madera y ciervos de cola blanca en abundancia (los cuales estaban más que dispuestos a comer lo que los colonos plantaran).

findings.location: source.html paragraph 7 ("Huge walnut, hickory, chestnuts, maples...")
findings.source_quote: Huge walnut, hickory, chestnuts, maples, white pines, and oaks, some six feet in diameter and over 100 feet tall, covered much of their new lands
findings.suggested_fix: "Hickory" was translated as "nogalinas", an uncommon term in Spanish. Use a more standard Spanish name such as "nogal" or "hickory" (kept as loanword) depending on audience. Suggested translation: "Enormes nogales, hickory (o nogalinas), castaños, arces, pinos blancos y robles..." Preserve HTML tags and attributes.
findings.translation_quote: Enormes nogales, nogalinas, castaños, arces, pinos blancos y robles, algunos de seis pies de diámetro y más de 100 pies de altura, cubrían gran parte de sus nuevas tierras (excepto algunos prados abiertos, dejados por los nativos americanos, y humedales).
